Question: Training use (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: whether your data improves future models (off by default for API traffic)

Question: Retention (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: whether your data is stored at all after the request is served

Question: Violation rate (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: harmful content that got through

Question: False refusal rate (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: legitimate requests that were blocked

Question: Jailbreak (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: the user tries to talk the model out of its constraints

Question: Direct prompt injection (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: the user embeds instructions that override the system prompt

Question: Indirect prompt injection (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: untrusted content the agent retrieves (a web page, a document, a tool result) carries instructions aimed at the model

Question: First-party API (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: your application must emit the audit trail; Anthropic provides request IDs to correlate

Question: Bedrock (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: CloudTrail records every InvokeModel call natively; enable model invocation logging for payloads if policy requires

Question: Vertex (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: Cloud Audit Logs record API activity; Cloud Logging for payloads if enabled

Question: Autonomous (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: low-impact, reversible actions (draft a reply, summarize a document)

Question: Approve-before-execute (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: the agent proposes, a human confirms (send the email, issue the refund)

Question: Human-performs (governance safety and risk management)
Answer: the agent only recommends; a human executes (medical decisions, legal filings)

Question: Value (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: what outcome improves, by how much

Question: Cost (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: what it costs to run, per outcome

Question: Risk (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: what can go wrong, likelihood, blast radius, mitigation

Question: Time (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: when it ships, what phases, what gates

Question: Direct savings (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: handle-time reduction, deflection rate, throughput per head

Question: Revenue effects (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: faster response, longer coverage hours, higher conversion

Question: Cost of the system (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: inference, engineering, evaluation, ongoing operations (not just the API bill)

Question: Sensitivity (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: which assumption breaks the case first; usually adoption rate or escalation rate

Question: Quality (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: eval score at or above baseline; task success rate at or above the phase target

Question: Safety (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: red-team suite pass; violation and false-refusal rates within bounds

Question: Operations (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: alerting live, runbook written, on-call named, rollback tested

Question: Architecture decision records (ADRs) (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: what was chosen, what was rejected, why; the future team inherits your reasoning, not just your code

Question: Runbook (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: alert-by-alert response procedures: quality drift, cost spike, provider outage, guardrail trip, model deprecation notice

Question: System card / model use documentation (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: purpose, data flows, limitations, evaluation evidence; doubles as EU AI Act and procurement documentation

Question: Escalation matrix (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: who is paged for what, and who can authorize a rollback or kill switch

Question: Change log (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: every prompt, model, and tool change with its eval delta

Question: End users (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: what the assistant can and cannot do, how to phrase requests, how to escalate; short and example-driven

Question: Support and operations teams (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: how to read traces, common failure signatures, when to page engineering

Question: Reviewers (human-in-the-loop) (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: what they are approving, what to look for, how their decisions are logged

Question: Leadership (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: the dashboard: quality trend, cost per outcome, adoption, incident count

Question: Weekly (early life) (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: quality metrics, escalation rate, cost per outcome, top failure categories; feed real failures back into the eval set

Question: Monthly (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: stakeholder review against the original ROI case; adoption and satisfaction trends

Question: Quarterly (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: model version review (anything deprecating?), risk re-tiering, guardrail effectiveness (both violation and false-refusal rates), and a decision: invest, maintain, or retire

Question: Incident-driven (stakeholder communication and lifecycle management)
Answer: every user-visible failure gets a lightweight postmortem; recurring patterns become eval cases and runbook entries
